exact_quote: It’s going to impact a bunch of office jobs that are about data summary, visual matching, pattern recognition, etc. And those are essentially about 5% of the economy.
question: Are the office tasks Acemoglu named (data summary, visual matching, pattern recognition) essentially about 5% of the US economy, as the share AI will impact, over the 10 years from 25 Feb 2025?
population: US office tasks of the kind named (data summary, visual matching, pattern recognition) that AI is expected to impact
denominator: The US economy (value-added or task-share, in the same framework Acemoglu used)
threshold: About 5% of the economy, over the 10-year window ending 25 Feb 2035
metric_unit: percent of the US economy (task or value-added share)
resolution_rule: Numeric 'about 5%.' The 10-year window is the same as the GDP claim on this page (25 Feb 2025–25 Feb 2035). KEPT if a published official or peer-reviewed task-share or value-added estimate of the office-task categories named (data summary, visual matching, pattern recognition) that AI impacts, as a share of the US economy, falls in 3–7% inclusive ('about 5%', frozen as ±2 percentage points). The Jan 2025 MIT Sloan wording of the same research ('only about 5% of tasks will be able to be profitably performed by AI within that time frame') is the same claim's task-share form; either a 3–7% task share or a 3–7% economy share, in that framework, counts. BROKEN if such an estimate exists and lies outside 3–7%. UNRESOLVABLE if no comparable published share exists at the deadline. This is not a claim that those occupations disappear (a separate, older Charter claim).
resolution_source: BLS / BEA occupational or value-added data, or a follow-up academic estimate in Acemoglu's task-exposure framework, covering the 2025–2035 window.
probability_note: No numerical probability was stated word for word by the original source; the claim is not in the Brier set.
basis: First-person quote, MIT Technology Review, 25 Feb 2025. Same 10-year horizon as the GDP claim in the same article. No numerical probability was stated.
base_rate_or_reference_class: His 2024 paper's task-exposure estimates; MIT Sloan 21 Jan 2025 ('only about 5% of tasks will be able to be profitably performed by AI within that time frame').
key_assumptions: The 10-year window of the same article applies to this share.
'About 5%' is resolved with a frozen ±2pp band.
A comparable published share will exist at the deadline.
update_triggers: A new Acemoglu or official task-share estimate away from 5%.
A public restatement by Acemoglu of the economy share.
